summary.zh: 焦糖化洋葱的深邃甜香，盖上烤脆的法棍与拉丝芝士。
summary.en: Deep caramelized sweetness under a gratinéed lid of crusty baguette and molten cheese.

ingredients.zh: 格鲁耶尔芝士 150 克（擦丝）
百里香 2 枝、香叶 1 片

ingredients.en: Salt and black pepper to taste

steps.zh: 洋葱顺纹切细丝，黄油入锅小火融化，下洋葱丝加一小撮盐。
steps.en: Slice onions thinly with the grain. Melt butter over low heat, add onions with a pinch of salt.

steps.zh: 小火慢炒 40-50 分钟，每隔几分钟翻动，直到洋葱变成深琥珀色焦糖状（这是汤的灵魂，急不得）。
steps.en: Cook low and slow 40–50 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until deep amber and caramelized — the soul of the soup cannot be rushed.

steps.zh: 淋入白葡萄酒刮起锅底焦香物质，煮至酒精挥发。
steps.en: Deglaze with white wine, scraping up the fond, and cook until the alcohol evaporates.

steps.zh: 加入牛肉高汤、百里香、香叶，小火炖 20 分钟，盐与黑胡椒调味。
steps.en: Add stock, thyme and bay leaf; simmer 20 minutes and season.
Toast baguette slices until golden and crisp.

steps.zh: 汤盛入耐热碗，放法棍片，铺满芝士，入烤箱上火 220°C 烤 5 分钟至芝士冒泡焦斑。
steps.en: Ladle soup into ovenproof bowls, top with toast and a mound of cheese; broil at 220°C for 5 minutes until bubbling and spotted.

tips.zh: 焦糖化是风味核心：洋葱要炒到「怀疑人生」的深褐色。
tips.en: Caramelization is everything: cook onions darker than feels comfortable.

tips.zh: 中途可加一小撮糖帮助焦糖化，但盐能更快逼出水分。
tips.en: A pinch of sugar aids browning; salt early to draw out moisture.

tips.zh: 用格鲁耶尔才有正宗拉丝效果，可用埃门塔尔替代。
tips.en: Gruyère gives the authentic cheese pull; Emmental works too.

failChecks.zh: 洋葱发苦：火太大炒焦了，焦糖化要全程小火耐心。
failChecks.en: Bitter onions? The heat was too high — caramelize gently.

failChecks.zh: 汤味单薄：洋葱焦糖化不足或高汤太淡，下次延长炒制时间。
failChecks.en: Thin flavor? Under-caramelized onions or weak stock — cook longer next time.

failChecks.zh: 面包沉底泡烂：法棍没烤脆或切太薄，需烤到坚硬再入汤。
failChecks.en: Soggy sunken bread? Toast it hard and cut thick slices.

culturalStory.zh: 洋葱汤的历史可追溯到罗马时代，曾是穷人的食物。现代版本定型于 18 世纪的巴黎，中央市场（Les Halles）的餐馆彻夜供应，成为凌晨收工的搬运工与狂欢者的「醒酒汤」。传说它因路易十五的深夜即兴烹饪而沾上了王室光环。如今，那一勺穿透芝士与法棍的浓汤，是巴黎小酒馆永恒的温暖开场。
culturalStory.en: Onion soup dates to Roman times as peasant fare; its modern form was set in 18th-century Paris, where Les Halles market bistros served it all night to porters and party-goers as the classic hangover cure. Legend even credits a midnight improvisation by Louis XV. Today, that spoon breaking through cheese and crust remains the eternal warm opening of a Parisian bistro.
